players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.signal: Phase 3 INTerpath-001 detailed results (ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium, accepted for publication in The New England Journal of Medicine): in 1,137 patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, after a median follow-up of 24.6 months, intismeran autogene plus KEYTRUDA reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% (HR=0.58; two-sided p<0.001) and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38% (HR=0.62; p=0.002) versus KEYTRUDA alone; two-year RFS was 82.2% versus 70.0%. After six months (following the immunization regimen) a pre-specified sensitivity analysis showed a 58% reduction in recurrence or death (HR=0.42). OS data are not yet mature but show a favorable trend; no new safety signals (grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events 14.2% versus 13.4%). The companies say they are engaging with regulatory authorities; the INTerpath program has nine Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials, including three ongoing Phase 3 trials in NSCLC.
